text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Tuesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The U.S. expects the NATO summit in Madrid to send a strong signal to the Baltic states that they will be seek membership in the alliance in the future.
- French President Jacques Chirac reassured President Algirdas Brazauskas that his country will support Lithuania's bid for European Union membership.
- Inflation in Lithuania in June was 0.2 percent.
- The official reserves of the Bank of Lithuania were $939.6 million at the end of June, a $56.3 million increase from the end of May.
- Mazheikiu Nafta started exporting diesel fuel via the port of Klaipeda on Monday. The firm signed an agreement with Klaipedos Nafta to export up to 50,000 tonnes per month.
- French President Jacques Chirac said on Monday that all three Baltic countries should join the European Union at the same time.
- The finance ministry has proposed to establish a price for a 42.875 million litas share issue of the state-run Agricultural Bank at 175 litas per share.
- The Bank of Lithuania will hold its third repo auction on Tuesday.
- Seventy percent of the respondents to a poll conducted by Vilmora supported the government's efforts to crack down on tax evasion.
